For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood that he felt he had missed himself.The quote is closely connected to Agassi’s own experience growing up. He started playing tennis as a young child and was pushed toward the sport by his father, Mike Agassi. His father had a clear dream for him: he wanted his son to become one of the best tennis players in the world.That dream eventually came true.Andre Agassi went on to become world No. 1 and won eight Grand Slam singles titles during his career. But reaching that level meant spending much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis.For a young child, that kind of life can leave little room for ordinary experiences. Instead of having complete freedom to decide how he wanted to spend his time, Agassi’s days were largely connected to tennis.That is where his famous quote becomes especially powerful.When he says he “gave up” his childhood, he is looking back at the years he spent becoming a professional athlete. But he is also talking about what those sacrifices eventually allowed him to do.His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family. It allowed him to be present as his children grew up.In other words, Agassi may have missed parts of his own childhood, but later he had the opportunity to sit beside his children and watch them experience theirs. For him, that became a kind of second chance.Fatherhood gave Andre Agassi a different way of looking at his past. When he watched Jaden and Jaz grow up, he could see the small moments of childhood from a parent’s point of view.He could watch them discover what they liked, make their own choices and develop personalities separate from their famous parents.Those moments were very different from the childhood Agassi had experienced.His early years were strongly connected to the tennis court. His father believed that constant practice and discipline were necessary if Andre Agassi was going to become a champion. That approach helped produce an incredible tennis career, but it also meant that Agassi’s childhood was far from ordinary.As a father, he wanted something different for his children.Instead of seeing childhood as preparation for a future career, Agassi wanted Jaden and Jaz to enjoy the years they were living through.That is one of the most important ideas behind his quote. He was not simply saying that he wanted to give his children more material things or better opportunities. He wanted to give them time.Time to grow. Time to explore. Time to make mistakes. Time to decide what they wanted for themselves.This became especially important because Agassi knew from personal experience how powerful parental expectations can be. He had spent years trying to become the player his father wanted him to be. As a parent, he had the chance to make sure his own children did not feel that same pressure.Steffi Graf’s role in the family’s story is important because she understood Agassi’s world better than almost anyone. Like her husband, Graf was introduced to tennis at a very young age and went on to become one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years at the top of women’s tennis before retiring in 1999. Agassi and Graf later married and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz.Together, they had something unusual in common: both parents knew exactly what it took to become a tennis champion, but they also knew the pressure that came with that journey.That understanding appears to have influenced the way they raised their children.Despite having two parents who were global tennis stars, Jaden and Jaz were not simply expected to follow the same path.Jaden developed a passion for baseball rather than choosing tennis as his main sport. Jaz has also been able to follow her own interests. Andre Agassi and Graf have supported their children without making their parents’ careers the center of their lives.That is particularly meaningful when viewed alongside Agassi’s quote.The couple had already achieved what many athletes spend their entire lives chasing. They did not need their children to continue that legacy for them.Instead, they could give their children something that both parents understood the value of: choice.Andre Agassi has also spoken warmly about Graf and the role she plays in his life. Their shared experience in professional sports gave them an understanding of the demands and sacrifices that come with elite competition.For their family, giving their children the freedom to choose their own paths became more important than creating another generation of tennis champions.At its heart, Agassi’s quote is about turning his own difficult experiences into something positive for his children.He cannot go back and change the childhood he had. He cannot erase the years of training, pressure and expectations that came with becoming a tennis player.But he can choose what kind of childhood his own children experience.That is what makes the quote about much more than tennis.Many parents work hard because they want their children to have opportunities they did not have themselves. Agassi’s story takes that idea one step further. His goal was not simply to provide his children with a comfortable life. He wanted to be present for the experiences that make childhood special.His words also show that parenthood can change the way people understand their own past.The same childhood that once felt difficult to Agassi became part of what helped him understand his children better. His experiences taught him what pressure can feel like, which may have made him more aware of the importance of giving his own children freedom.And Steffi Graf was there beside him, bringing her own experience as a former champion and a parent.Together, Agassi and Graf chose not to make their children’s lives about living up to their parents’ names. They allowed Jaden and Jaz to build identities of their own.That may be the most powerful part of Agassi’s words.He spent his childhood becoming a tennis champion. But when he became a father, he did not want his children to spend their childhood becoming something for him.He wanted to watch them simply be children.So, when Agassi says, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” he is not only talking about sacrifice. He is talking about perspective, presence and love.He gave years of his life to tennis. Those years helped him become a champion and eventually gave him the freedom to step back and focus on his family.For Agassi, one of the greatest rewards was not another trophy or achievement. It was being able to watch his children grow up on their own terms, with Graf by his side.That is what makes his quote so relatable. Parenthood does not allow us to rewrite our own childhoods, but it can give us the chance to create a different childhood for the next generation.
Article Summary: Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf have two children, Jaden and Jaz. Agassi’s famous quote, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children�'s childhood,” offers a look at how becoming a parent changed his view of his own life. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood.

Article Title: Alaska used rotenone to eliminate invasive pike from an entire lake; the pike vanished, and 6,836 Arctic char were later stocked to rebuild the native fishery
Article Text:
Representative image

Why northern pike are a problem in Alaska

Rotenone: a targeted, temporary reset

Alaska eliminates invasive pike and restocks lake with 6,836 Arctic char

Stormy Lake: a case study in eradication and recovery

Other lakes, similar stories

Why Arctic char matter

Balancing restoration with public concern

A tool, not a silver bullet

In a remote corner of Southcentral Alaska, state biologists carried out a dramatic restoration: they treated an entire lake with rotenone, a plant-derived piscicide, to wipe out an invasive population of northern pike. After the treatment, post-surveys confirmed the pike were gone. The next step was rebuilding what had been lost. In June 2013, the Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G) stocked 6,836 hatchery-reared Arctic char fingerlings into the now pike-free lake, jump-starting the recovery of a native fishery that had been pushed out by the predator. This account draws on ADF&G’s technical reports and project summaries documenting the rotenone treatment and restocking. Read on to know more:Northern pike are not native to most of Southcentral Alaska. They were illegally introduced into several lakes in the mid-20th century and have since spread through connected waterways, especially as warming temperatures and changing hydrology make it easier for them to move and survive. As apex predators, pike eat large quantities of native fish, including salmon, trout, grayling and char. In some lakes, they have all but replaced native sport fish, collapsing local angling opportunities and altering food webs.ADF&G describes pike as a major threat to endemic fish populations and has pursued a mix of suppression and eradication strategies depending on the waterbody. In isolated lakes where pike can be completely removed, the agency has turned to rotenone as the most practical and efficient tool.Rotenone is a naturally occurring compound derived from certain tropical plants. It has been used for decades in fisheries management to remove unwanted fish from lakes and streams. When applied at carefully calculated concentrations, it blocks oxygen uptake in fish gills, killing fish while leaving most other aquatic organisms unaffected. The chemical breaks down relatively quickly in sunlight and warm water; in many Alaskan projects, detectable levels drop to near zero within weeks to months.There are only two proven methods to eradicate invasive fish from lakes: completely draining the waterbody or using a piscicide like rotenone. For most lakes, draining is not feasible, making rotenone the default option for full eradication. Before treatment, ADF&G typically relocates any desirable native fish, such as salmon or trout, to safe holding areas or other lakes, then treats the target lake and its outlet streams to ensure no pike survive.Stormy Lake, near Anchorage, is one of the clearest examples of this approach. In fall 2012, ADF&G treated Stormy Lake and its outlet creek with liquid rotenone to eradicate an established northern pike population. Post-treatment evaluations—including netting and electrofishing surveys, found no surviving pike, confirming the treatment’s success.Once the rotenone had fully degraded (by late January 2013, about four months after application), the agency began restocking. Native fish that had been held in offsite net pens were reintroduced in March 2013, and on June 17, 2013, ADF&G stocked 6,836 hatchery-reared Arctic char fingerlings into Stormy Lake. These char were of mixed Stormy Lake and Dolly Varden Lake parentage, helping to re-establish a robust, genetically diverse population.The project’s final report, published in ADF&G’s Sport Fish Research series, describes the effort as a successful model for eradicating invasive pike and restoring native fisheries.Stormy Lake is not unique. ADF&G has used rotenone to remove pike from multiple lakes in the Anchorage and Mat-Su areas, including Sand Lake, Anderson Lake and Kings Lake. In each case, the sequence is similar: treat the lake, confirm pike are gone, then restock with native species such as rainbow trout, Arctic char and grayling.For example, after rotenone treatments in 2020, Anderson and Kings lakes were declared pike-free and added to the Northern Cook Inlet stocking program in 2021. Both lakes were restocked with rainbow trout, restoring sport fisheries that had been lost to pike predation. In Anchorage, pike have been eradicated from all but one of five lakes where they were confirmed, with Lower Fire Lake remaining a management challenge.Arctic char are a prized native species in Alaska, valued both ecologically and by anglers. They thrive in cold, clear lakes and are an important part of the natural food web. In lakes where pike have been removed, char are often a key restocking target because they can grow to good size, support recreational fishing and help re-establish a more natural predator–prey balance.In Stormy Lake, the 6,836 char stocked in 2013 were intended to re-create a self-sustaining population that could eventually support a catch-and-release or limited-harvest fishery. Monitoring in subsequent years showed that char, along with other restocked natives, were surviving and growing, indicating the lake was returning to a healthier, pre-pike state.The use of rotenone is not without controversy. Killing all fish in a lake, even temporarily, can be unsettling for nearby residents and anglers. ADF&G addresses these concerns through public meetings, environmental assessments and detailed explanations of why the treatment is necessary and how risks are managed.Agency biologists say allowing pike to remain in the lakes can pose a greater threat to native biodiversity and long-term fishing opportunities. In lakes where pike have become established, native fish may not recover without removing the invasive population completely. When used correctly, rotenone can help achieve this reset, allowing fisheries to be rebuilt with native species.While rotenone has proven effective in isolated lakes, it is not a solution for every pike-infested waterbody. In large, connected systems like much of the Mat-Su Valley, complete eradication is currently impossible because pike can simply move back in from untreated areas. There, ADF&G focuses on suppression, using gillnets, targeted rotenone applications in key tributaries, and liberal harvest rules to keep pike numbers down in priority fisheries.Projects like Stormy Lake show where eradication is still feasible: in relatively closed basins where pike can be fully removed and native fish reintroduced. For those lakes, the combination of rotenone treatment and strategic stocking—like the 6,836 Arctic char released in 2013, offers a path back to a more natural, resilient fishery. For Alaska’s fisheries managers, such projects demonstrate that invasive predators can sometimes be removed and native fish populations rebuilt when the conditions are right. Share your thoughts on the story in the comment section.
Article Summary: Northern pike are not native to most of Southcentral Alaska. They were illegally introduced into several lakes in the mid-20th century. Pike eat large quantities of native fish, including salmon, trout, grayling and char. They have all but replaced native sport fish, collapsing local angling opportunities.

Article Title: Apple's new CEO John Ternus may have just told millions of professionals around the world that LinkedIn is 'not important' when you are ...
Article Text:
Limited information on Apple CEO John Ternus’ LinkedIn profile

John Ternus recently joined Twitter

Apple’s new CEO John Ternus may have just told millions of professionals around the world that LinkedIn is 'not important' when you are trying to reach the top of the tech industry. John Ternus became Apple CEO on September 1 after more than 25 years at the company, but his LinkedIn profile still does not list him as CEO. Instead, the profile identifies Ternus as Apple’s vice president of hardware engineering. It also leaves out much of his career at Apple, including his involvement with major products such as the Apple Watch and AirPods.For someone who has risen to lead one of the world’s biggest technology companies, his limited LinkedIn presence is notable.John Ternus’ LinkedIn page contains only a small amount of information about his professional career. It lists his time at Apple and a four-year stint as an engineer at Virtual Research Inc. The profile also mentions his mechanical engineering degree from the University of Pennsylvania. Apart from a profile picture and Apple as a followed interest, there is little else.Most notably, the profile has not yet been updated to show his new position as Apple CEO. Apple’s internal pages were updated immediately after Ternus took over from Tim Cook on September 1.While Ternus has not made much of his LinkedIn profile, he recently joined X (formerly Twitter). His first post was simply “hello.” The post had received over 81 million views and 523,000 likes as of the time of the report.Tesla and X chief Elon Musk replied to Ternu’s Hello post writing, “Congrats!"”before following up with an additional comment noting, “New Apple CEO posting on X”.Notably, Ternus currently follows only three accounts: Apple, Tim Cook and Apple senior vice president of marketing Greg Joswiak.
Article Summary: John Ternus’ LinkedIn page contains only a small amount of information about his professional career. Apart from a profile picture and Apple as a followed interest, there is little else. The profile has not yet been updated to show his new position as Apple CEO. Apple’s internal pages were updated immediately after Ternu took over from Tim Cook on September 1.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

RCB register their second win

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Academia and algorithm: When your professor pops up on your feed
Article Text:
Ahead of Teacher’s Day, professor creators speak to us about dealing with Gen Z, social media and respect (AI image for representation only)

‘Helps understand students better’

From aesthetics to humour, professors carve their social media niche (Pics: @dr.drishti_kalra, @prasoliterature)

When profs break the ‘serious’ stereotype

They follow trends and understand students in their own language (Pics: @wanderlustsoul_rj, @textsubtext)

Keeping the student-teacher balance

The relationship is still built in the classroom, but social media can make the first interaction less formal and intimidating. If my students feel that they can approach me more easily because they have seen me online, I think that’s a wonderful thing Taruna Tokas, assistant professor

Social media, however, can blur some boundaries, and professor creators have noticed the shift too (Pics: @prasoliterature, @ishita.creates)

‘Respect grows when you meet students where they are’





If you thought content creation on campus is for students only, think again. These professors are turning their college experience into mini vlogs, tips and tricks, sharing their side of life in academia. Ahead of Teacher’s Day, they speak to us about dealing with Gen Z, social media and respect.For many teachers, social media is offering new insights into student behaviour beyond academia. Rajnandani Yadav, assistant professor at a private university in Noida, shares, “It has helped me understand students’ interests, communication styles and the changing digital environment they are part of. I have interacted with students who are actively creating content. They often ask what opportunities, exposure and growth they can get by entering this field. ”Taruna Tokas, assistant professor at Delhi University, agrees, saying, “Seeing students in a classroom is very different from understanding them as individuals. That has been a very interesting learning experience for me because you don’t necessarily have to write a research paper every time you want to understand something.Social media can teach you a great deal simply by listening to what people are saying. For me, it has given me a better sense of what students expect from their educators and the larger learning system. ”Sonal Chauhan, assistant professor of English at Delhi University, was inspired by a chef who shared a day in their life. “The way I found myself interested in knowing what a chef’s day looks like, someone might have similar curiosity about an assistant professor’s life. The stereotype was that we are meant to be private, a little mysterious. I did not feel the need to conform to that. I posted a vlog the very next day and it got millions of views in a day. ”Ishita Arora, professor of Mass Communication at a private university, says, “It’s a fair concern in a profession like teaching to be apprehensive about being “visible” online. Primarily, because being a content creator does not “suit” the image of a teacher and the profession requires a certain formality. There was a slight awkwardness at first, but then one day, a fellow faculty member mentioned my content and appreciated my efforts. Although a few of them did pass some sarcastic remarks, the overall response was good.”Social media, however, can blur some boundaries, and professor creators have noticed the shift too. For young professors, navigating the dynamic with college students can be tricky. Drishti Kalra, assistant professor at DU, notes, “Being online has not changed the student teacher equation as much as people assume. Only the setting has moved from offline to online. That said, as a female teacher, there are students who will try to test the boundaries. ‘Ma’am, coffee pe chalein? Ma’am, can we be friends?’ In response, one keeps the line thick and visible and does not respond to everything.”Echoing a similar sentiment, Rajnandani says, “I believe the balance comes through clearly defined boundaries. I enjoy connecting with my students, but I ensure that the professional relationship is always maintained.” Ishita adds, “Seeing me engage on the same platforms as my students made them more comfortable around me. It doesn’t erase the teacher-student gap, but it softens its edges. A student who thinks you might actually understand their world is more willing to let you into it, even just a little, and that matters for learning. ”“To help students evolve into well-rounded individuals, a professor’s role must extend beyond a lecture. Respect grows when you tear down unnecessary walls, meet students where they are, and make them feel seen,” Taruna adds.Sonal explains the criticism, “I’ve been told that posting about enjoying my mornings misrepresents how demanding the job is, and that I should instead show how hard it is. I’ve been asked to take posts down and stay off social media during my probation in case I said something controversial. One senior professor even told me to stop altogether, saying young girls were approaching her saying they wanted to do what I do – girls who, in her view, could have become doctors or officers,” she says.
Article Summary: For many teachers, social media is offering new insights into student behaviour beyond academia. For young professors, navigating the dynamic with college students can be tricky. Ahead of Teacher’s Day, they speak to us about dealing with Gen Z and respect.

Article Title: Woman found dead inside Delhi hotel room, husband unconscious
Article Text:
A woman was allegedly stabbed to death by her husband inside a north Delhi hotel





NEW DELHI: A woman was allegedly stabbed to death by her husband inside a hotel in north Delhi’s Lahori Gate area Thursday. Police suspect the man also attempted suicide after the killing.A preliminary inquiry has revealed that the couple had a family-related dispute.The woman, Shivani Kumari from Samastipur, Bihar, was married to Prakash Singh (27) from Rajasthan. Prakash runs a tea stall and Shivani worked in a beauty parlour in Old Delhi.The couple married about six months ago and initially lived together in Rajasthan. But after a month of staying with her husband, Shivani is suspected to have come to Delhi. She started staying on rent in Old Delhi.Police said Prakash travelled to Delhi Wednesday and contacted Shivani after reaching the city, asking her to meet him at the hotel. Investigators suspect he had planned the killing and subsequently intended to take his own life. The couple checked into a hotel in the Lahori Gate area around 3.30 pm.The incident came to light around 5.20 am Thursday when the hotel staff alerted police after finding Shivani lying in a pool of blood inside the room.A police team reached the spot and found Prakash too. He was unconscious. Both were taken to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared Shivani brought dead. Prakash is under treatment. Police said Shivani had two stab wounds.Investigators suspect Prakash stabbed her at night before consuming some poisonous substance. Police are waiting for his condition to stabilise before questioning him.Investigators have collected evidence from the hotel room and are examining CCTV footage from the premises and surrounding areas to reconstruct their movements. They are also questioning hotel employees and others who may have interacted with the couple. The cops are also probing who brought the knife.The incident comes amid a series of murders reported in hotels in central and north Delhi.In March, a 24-year-old Delhi University student was arrested for killing a woman at a hotel in north Delhi’s Lahori Gate.In June last year, a 29-year-old woman was found murdered in a hotel room in central Delhi’s Paharganj.The same month, another woman was killed in a Paharganj hotel over suspicion of an extramarital affair.
Article Summary: The woman, Shivani Kumari from Samastipur, Bihar, was married to Prakash Singh (27) from Rajasthan. Police suspect the man also attempted suicide after the killing. A preliminary inquiry has revealed that the couple had a family-related dispute.

Article Title: Theatre Review: A rock opera that makes the Mahabharata pulse with new life
Article Text:
Jaya: The Victory reimagines the timeless Mahabharata through an innovative rock opera lens. With Ashutosh Phatak's dynamic score harmonizing rock and classical elements, the production resonates with modern audiences. Sandeep Kanjilal's impactful lyrics illuminate the characters’ emotional journeys. Stellar performances by Sherrin Varghese and Megan Murray as Krishna and Draupadi enhance its dramatic effect, ensuring that this ancient tale remains strikingly relevant for contemporary viewers.

Should you watch it?





Jaya: The Victory – A Rock Musical of the Mahabharata (Drama, Musical)Critic's rating: 3.5 starsCast: Tirthankar Poddar, Sherrin Varghese, Megan Murray, Vikrant Chaturvedi, Varun Narayan, Danny Sura, Sid Makkar, Asif Ali Beg, Mehmood Curmally, Keshia B, Sunayana Sarkar and Ujjayinee RoyDirector: Lillete Dubey Duration: 2 hours 15 minutesLanguage: EnglishThere's a particular thrill in watching an epic as old as time crack open into electric guitar riffs, melodious numbers and thundering percussion, and that's exactly what Lillete Dubey's Jaya: The Victory delivers. This rock opera retelling of the Mahabharata, seen through Yudhishthira's conflicted conscience, doesn't just modernise myth; it makes it pulse.If there's one reason to buy a ticket, it's the score. Ashutosh Phatak's music doesn't merely accompany the storytelling; it carries it. The songs swing between brooding, anthemic rock numbers and quieter, classical-inflected melodies without ever feeling tonally mismatched. Sandeep Kanjilal's lyrics give weight to Yudhishthira's moral spirals, Duryodhana's hunger and Karna's tragic resignation, turning each soliloquy into something closer to a power ballad.Sherrin Varghese, as Krishna, brings a magnetic, almost mischievous gravitas to every number he's part of, while the delightful Megan Murray, as Draupadi, is vocally fierce. Her songs land with the kind of conviction that makes the theatre fall silent.Tirthankar Poddar, aka 2Blue, as Yudhishthira, anchors the production with a voice that carries doubt and dharma in equal measure.The choreography, a striking marriage of Kathak's fluid grace and Kalaripayattu's raw martial precision, gives the battle sequences a visual charge rarely seen on the Indian stage. The production recasts myth as spectacle, with just enough irreverence to keep it from feeling reverential to a fault.Jaya: The Victory is an ambitious piece of theatre that largely earns its scale. The narrative occasionally takes a back seat to its own visual and sonic flourishes, but when the songs hit—and they hit often—you forgive the show almost everything else. In an age where power, greed and righteousness still dominate the headlines, Lillete Dubey's Mahabharata doesn't feel like ancient history. It feels like the present, set to a killer soundtrack.Yes, if you're looking for a bold, musically driven reimagining of the Mahabharata.
Article Summary: Jaya: The Victory reimagines the timeless Mahabharata through an innovative rock opera lens. With Ashutosh Phatak's dynamic score harmonizing rock and classical elements, the production resonates with modern audiences. Sandeep Kanjilal's impactful lyrics illuminate the characters’ emotional journeys. Stellar performances by Sherrin Varghese and Megan Murray enhance its dramatic effect.

Article Title: Mumbai’s anime fandom comes alive
Article Text:
‘Cosplay lets me step into the world of a character’

‘Anime gives young audiences emotional stories’





Mumbai went full anime mode recently, with nearly 50,000 fans showing up as their favourite characters, comparing costumes, swapping recommendations and finding fellow fans. The fourth edition of Anime India Mumbai brought cosplay, gaming, music and fan art together, showing just how far anime has travelled from niche fandom to mainstream youth culture.For many fans, cosplay is more than dressing up — it is a way to become part of the stories they love. “I cosplay because it lets me step into the world of a character I love. For a few hours, you are not just watching the story; you are part of it,” says Rithvik Sharma, who attended the convention dressed as one of their favourite anime characters. Pratham Jha adds, “Spider-Man is the hero I grew up with. Today, getting to dress like him and meet other fans makes the whole experience even more special. ”For Anime India co-founder Mishaal Wanvari, the growing response reflects how deeply anime has entered India’s youth culture. “There are more than 100 million anime fans in India. After COVID, anime saw a huge spike, and people now want to meet, engage and celebrate that fandom together,” he says, adding that young audiences have played a major role in its growth.“Anime gives young audiences emotional stories and characters they can connect with deeply. This event is about bringing that community together under one roof.”One Piece is what got me into anime, so I really wanted to dress as one of its characters, and Nami was my choice. This is my first time attending an event like this, and I’m so excited to see so many others who love anime like I do– Hrishita Kothari, a cosplayer.Spider-Man is the hero I grew up with. Today, getting to dress like him and meet other fans makes the whole experience even more special – Pratham Jha, student.

Article Title: Mumbai: Ferry boat breaks down mid-sea near Gateway of India, all 38 onboard safe
Article Text:
A ferry boat named Anvari broke down mid-sea near Gateway of India.





MUMBAI: A mishap was averted at the Gateway of India on Thursday night after a ferry boat broke down mid-sea. It was towed by another ferry boat and all 38 people onboard were brought to shore safely. No untoward incident took place.The incident occurred around 8.30pm when the 'Anvari' ferry, which had left for a half an hour joyride from the Gateway of India, broke down suddenly while returning. The boat was stranded about 1.5 nautical miles away from the shore.There were 38 people on board, including 34 passengers and four crew members. Police found that another ferry boat, 'Azad Hind', near the stranded boat and which towed the stranded ferry to safety.
Article Summary: The 'Anvari' ferry had left for a half an hour joyride from the Gateway of India. The boat was stranded about 1.5 nautical miles away from the shore. Police found that another ferry boat, 'Azad Hind', near the stranded boat and towed the stranded ferry to safety.

Article Title: Policemen lived in Bhuleshwar BMC school for 5 years; issued notice to vacate, says civic official
Article Text:
Mumbai:





Several policemen resided in a BMC school in Bhuleshwar’s Gulalwadi for five years while students from standards one to seven attended classes on the premises.When contacted, deputy municipal commissioner Prachi Jambhekar said, “These rooms were given to the police force during the Covid pandemic and we are giving them a notice to clear it. ” Jambekhar shared with TOI an image on Thursday evening showing that the rooms in the school had been cleared.A teacher at the school said, “We asked the cops many times not to roam around in their underwear with so many children around, but they didn’t listen.” The school is managed by an NGO and has a total of 47 students across Gujarati and Marathi mediums.A senior police officer confirmed to TOI: “Two rooms in the school were allotted to the SRPF. The SRPF personnel deployed at different places used it as their barracks.”The matter first came to light when Chaitali Doshi, an independent educational activist now aligned with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), posted on social media about the potential safety hazard of having adult men living around school-going children.Doshi said, “I went to the school to survey its condition when one of the NGO workers working in the school told me about the policemen staying inside.When I entered the room, I saw one policeman lying in his underwear, and this was while classes were in session right beside them.” The cops were originally accommodated on the third and fourth floors of the school. However, due to construction work on the upper floors, they were shifted to the ground floor, next to the classrooms.Doshi added, “There was garbage like derelict furniture piled up in classrooms, and a library which scarcely had one book that did not have its pages ripped or wasn’t completely covered in dust and grime.”Classrooms have also been given out to govt officials conducting SIR work, while a room has been allotted to govt officials conducting a polio eradication drive. Doshi said, “The school is in a horrifying condition. On top of it, so much of the building has been given out for non-academic work.”(Inputs by Mateen Hafeez)

The matter first came to light when an independent educational activist now aligned with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) posted on social media about the potential safety hazard.
